signal: HSI launched AI-powered corrective actions and image hazard recognition, acquired HandsHQ, and earned IACET accreditation, expanding its EHS compliance platform.

email.body1:
Lori, saw HSI launched AI-powered corrective actions and image hazard recognition, plus the HandsHQ acquisition.

Expanding the platform that fast usually means more EHS buyers in play than the team can reach, and that is where pipeline leaks. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for HSI off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Lori, quick follow-up for HSI.

With the AI launches and HandsHQ widening the offering, the pipeline target probably grew faster than the team can. Most BD leaders cannot say exactly how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings HSI needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Lori, last bit of proof for HSI.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how HSI's reply rate likely compares to peer EHS and compliance teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
